To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

“The direction of causality between growth and inflation is non-uniform and that the low world inflation environment has implications for the distribution of real growth opportunities among countries”.

the direction of the causality between inflation an economic growth is non-unidirectional and non-uniform across all countries, and that the industrialized countries will be the net beneficiaries of the low inflation regime.

the relationship between inflationary expectations and economic growth in a large number of industrial and developing countries is non-uniform and that the low inflation regime which is now emerging will on average redistribute real growth opportunities away from the developing towards the industrial countries.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following issues: first, what are the implications of low inflation for the cross-country pattern of economic growth, and second, what are the policy implications of our results for the industrialized and developing countries.
the question of how the world economy is likely to adjust to a low world inflation regime.
the relationship between inflation, economic growth, and international competitiveness, which are all interrelated.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there exists no simple, uni-dimensional, universal relationship between inflation and economic performance.

the relationship between inflationary expectations and growth is not uniform across countries, but that a large majority of the world economy is characterized by a uni- or bi-causal relationship between the two variables.
the relationship between inflation an economic growth is complex and non-uniform across different country groupings.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there exists a strong relationship between the two variables in the industrial countries and the developing countries.
the relationship between inflation, growth and development is complex and non-uniform across the world.
the low world inflation environment will have an overall adverse effect on the developing countries.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a need for a rethinking of the inflation and growth nexus.
the world is moving towards a low inflation regime.
the relationship between inflationary expectations and growth opportunities is non-uniform and non-linear.
